A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FEA-Bench. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching content relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark statistics and LLM evaluations on FEA-Bench and its lite subset, including the experiments in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds Agentless and Agentless-Lite evaluations in Table 5.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, task inputs, filtering rules, and proposed generation formats remain unchanged. Agentless and Agentless-Lite are added comparison methods, not modifications to the proposed approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,401 tasks from 83 Python repositories and the same 200-task lite subset. The new framework evaluations use that existing subset. Appendix A.3 proposes a future verified subset but reports no completed addition.

E2.justification: v2 substantially extends comparison scope from directly prompted LLMs to agent frameworks. Table 5 evaluates Agentless-Lite with five models and Agentless with GPT-4o, o1-mini, and o1, alongside Oracle and BM25. v1 only cites Agentless; its original evaluated comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The documented subsets, evaluation metrics, context limits, and generation settings remain unchanged. Table 5 uses the existing lite subset and resolved/application metrics; v2 does not specify separate agent budgets or other new protocol settings.

E4.justification: The context-length, Natural-versus-Patch, repository-category, and component-complexity analyses are unchanged. The new framework performance comparison does not introduce a separately specified ablation, robustness test, or error-analysis procedure.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the single-generation description and provide no repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new framework comparison adds no statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results remain unchanged. Table 5 adds framework scores and lite-subset edit-application rates: for example, o1 with Agentless achieves 14.0% resolved and 90.5% applied, versus 5.0% and 33.5% with BM25. These are newly reported framework comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The task definitions and mathematical content remain unchanged. Neither version contains a theoretical contribution with theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a feature-implementation benchmark spanning 83 repositories and evidence that current LLMs struggle with these tasks. The agent results do not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 newly connects agent performance gains to successful edit application and interprets the frameworks as offering no significant overall advantage over Oracle. The limitations explicitly acknowledge Python-only coverage, and Appendix A.3 adds a future expert-verified subset plan.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B retain the construction instructions, prompt templates, hardware, model versions, sampling parameters, and generation limits. Code-release information is unchanged, and no agent-specific implementation or configuration details are added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Luo et al. (2025), a survey of LLM agents, and a reference to SWE-bench Verified for the proposed future subset. Agentless, already cited in v1, gains an empirical comparison; the broader novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical and terminology corrections, clarifies filtering language, inserts Section 6.3, expands the limitations, and adds acknowledgments. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, renumbers the appendix tables, and shifts existing figures and text through the layout. Existing figure content and table structures are preserved; notably, Figures 5 and 6 move to later pages.

improvement.justification: The new framework comparisons extend the benchmark's empirical usefulness beyond direct prompting, while the explicit Python-only limitation clarifies applicability. These are useful, limited gains. Missing agent-specific configurations and uncertainty estimates constrain the conclusions, especially the claim of no significant advantage over Oracle.
